# Overview

A Gaussian Markov network simulation has four conceptually separate layers (@eq-pipeline). For non-Gaussian expression data, a fifth observation layer can be added (e.g. Poisson–log-normal counts or zero-inflated measurements).

$$
G \longrightarrow W(G) \longrightarrow \Omega \succ 0
\longrightarrow X_i \sim \mathcal{N}_p(\mu_i,\Omega^{-1})
$$ {#eq-pipeline}

Here $G$ is an **undirected** graph, $W(G)$ a symmetric weighted matrix with the same off-diagonal support, $\Omega$ a strictly positive-definite precision, and $X_i$ an expression profile. The **graph** and the **precision** must not be conflated: a binary adjacency is almost never itself positive definite, so a separate weighting and regularisation step is required.

This vignette covers **undirected** Gaussian Markov / precision-graph simulation only.

DeCovarT’s synthetic helpers follow the same split ([synthetic scenarios vignette](synthetic-scenarios.html)): `generate_random_network_skeleton()` draws $G$, and `build_normalised_precision()` completes it to $\Omega\succ 0$ by an affine spectral shift.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-pipeline
%%| fig-cap: "Undirected simulation pipeline from topology to observations (optional observation layer dashed)."
flowchart LR
  G["Undirected graph G"] --> W["Signed weights W(G)"]
  W --> Omega["SPD precision Ω"]
  Omega --> Latent["Latent Gaussian X"]
  Mu["Mean design μ"] --> Latent
  Latent --> Obs["Observation layer"]
  Latent -.-> Obs
```

# Evidence from the literature

@tbl-studies summarises how recent simulation studies combine topology, precision construction, and mean / observation models.

| Source | Graph structures | Precision construction | Mean / observation | Purpose |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| PLNnetwork [@chiquetVariationalInferenceSparse2018] | Erdős–Rényi, preferential attachment, affiliation | $\Omega = vG + \operatorname{diag}(\lvert\lambda_{\min}(vG)\rvert + u)$ | Latent log-abundance $XB$; compositional / multinomial counts | Count-network estimators under compositionality |
| SILGGM [@zhangSILGGMExtensivePackage2018] | Band, hub, Erdős–Rényi, scale-free via `huge` | Package covariance / precision simulation | Centred Gaussian; focus on precision entries | Large-$p$ inferential and computational stress tests |
| BLGGM [@wuEstimatingHeterogeneousGene2022] | Block mixtures of dense, circle, star, signed modules | Module matrices with structured signed off-diagonals | Cell-type-specific $\mu_k$, $\Omega_k$; expression-dependent dropout | Joint clustering, heterogeneous networks, zero inflation |
| Structure learning / modular GRNs [@federicoStructureLearningGene2023] | Modular and related hierarchical graphs | GGM linked to each graph | Shared structure across related networks; $n\ll p$ | Modular constraints and information sharing |

: Literature survey of undirected graph → precision → observation designs. {#tbl-studies}

Several conclusions follow.

1.  **Band** is not intrinsically a random-graph model: its support is usually deterministic once the bandwidth is fixed (edge weights and signs may still be random). Hub constructions are often partly deterministic as well. Erdős–Rényi, preferential attachment, and stochastic block models are genuinely stochastic.
2.  A positive off-diagonal entry in $\Omega$ encodes a **negative** partial correlation (@eq-partial-cor). Uniformly positive precision weights therefore induce uniformly negative edgewise partial correlations; random or signed biological weights are needed when activation-like and inhibition-like associations matter.
3.  These models target **undirected** conditional dependence. Federico and colleagues prefer a Markov-network representation when observational data do not justify edge directionality [@federicoStructureLearningGene2023].

$$
\rho_{jk\mid -\{j,k\}}
=
-\frac{\Omega_{jk}}{\sqrt{\Omega_{jj}\Omega_{kk}}}
$$ {#eq-partial-cor}

# Graph structure generators

@tbl-topologies compares the main **undirected** topology families used in GGM benchmarks, with R entry points.

| Structure | Definition and controls | R entry points | Advantages | Limitations |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| **Erdős–Rényi** | Each edge present independently with probability $q$; $q=d_{\mathrm{avg}}/(p-1)$ targets average degree | `huge::huge.generator(graph="random")` [@R-huge]; `BDgraph::graph.sim(graph="random")` [@R-BDgraph] | Exact sparsity control in expectation; few nuisance parameters | Narrow degree distribution; little modular organisation |
| **Band / AR** | Edge $j$–$k$ if $1\le\lvert j-k\rvert\le b$ | `huge.generator(graph="band")` [@R-huge]; `BDgraph::bdgraph.sim(graph="AR(1)")` / `"AR(2)"` [@R-BDgraph] | Local dependence and controlled max degree | Artificial gene ordering; no hubs or modules |
| **Hub / star** | $g$ groups; one centre linked to remaining members | `huge.generator(graph="hub")` [@R-huge]; `graph.sim(graph="hub")` / `"star"` [@R-BDgraph] | Stress-tests high-degree regulators | Pure stars omit cross-talk |
| **Scale-free** | Preferential attachment (e.g. Barabási–Albert with $m$ edges per new node) | `huge.generator(graph="scale-free")` [@R-huge]; `graph.sim(graph="scale-free")` [@R-BDgraph]; DeCovarT `graph_model = "power_law"` | Heterogeneous degrees | Weak modularity under plain BA growth |
| **Cluster / SBM** | Within-block edge probability exceeds between-block | `huge.generator(graph="cluster")` [@R-huge]; `graph.sim(graph="cluster")` [@R-BDgraph]; DeCovarT `graph_model = "stochastic_block_model"` | Pathway / module structure | Equal blocks and homogeneous $P$ can be unrealistically regular |
| **Small-world / lattice / circle** | High clustering with short paths, or fixed neighbourhoods | `graph.sim(graph="smallworld")`, `"lattice"`, `"circle"` [@R-BDgraph] | Local modules and spatial organisation | Narrow degrees; needs a defensible ordering |

: Topology families for undirected GGM simulation (R-focused). {#tbl-topologies}

## Package roles (R)

-   **`huge`** [@R-huge] — compact end-to-end GGM benchmark via
    `huge.generator()`: topology, SPD precision, covariance, and
    $\mathcal{N}_p$ samples. Supports random, hub, cluster, band, and
    scale-free graphs [@zhangSILGGMExtensivePackage2018].
-   **`BDgraph`** [@R-BDgraph; @BDgraph2019] — broadest undirected
    simulation surface: `graph.sim()` for topologies; `bdgraph.sim()` for
    data (including a `mean` argument and non-Gaussian families);
    `rgwish()` for G-Wishart draws that respect graph-constrained zeros.

# Positive-definiteness strategies

@tbl-pd contrasts constructions that turn a weighted support $W$ into $\Omega\succ 0$.

| Construction | Formula | SPD? | Preserves exact support? | Behaviour |
|--------------|--------------|-------------:|----------------:|--------------|
| Uniform spectral shift | $\Omega=W+\max(0,\varepsilon-\lambda_{\min}(W))I$ | Yes | Yes | Same shift on every eigenvalue; off-diagonals unchanged |
| `huge` / PLN-style loading | Diagonal load from $\lvert\lambda_{\min}\rvert$, baseline, and $u$ | Yes | Yes | $v$ sets edge magnitude; loading sets conditioning [@chiquetVariationalInferenceSparse2018] |
| Graph Laplacian / M-matrix | $\Omega=L_G+\varepsilon I$ | Yes | Yes | Off-diagonals non-positive ⇒ all edgewise partial correlations positive |
| G-Wishart | $\Omega\sim W_G(b,D)$ | Yes | Yes | Heterogeneous random weights; `BDgraph::rgwish()` [@R-BDgraph] |
| Eigenvalue clipping | Clip $\Lambda$ then reconstruct $Q\Lambda Q^{\top}$ | Yes | **No** | Fills structural zeros |
| Nearest PD projection | e.g. `Matrix::nearPD()` [@R-Matrix] | Yes | **No** (in general) | Repair tool, not a support-preserving truth |

: Positive-definiteness constructions for graph-constrained precisions. {#tbl-pd}

## Why the uniform spectral shift is attractive

If $W=Q\Lambda Q^{\top}$, then (@eq-spectral-shift)

$$
W+cI = Q(\Lambda+cI)Q^{\top}.
$$ {#eq-spectral-shift}

Every eigenvalue increases by $c$, while every off-diagonal of $W$ is unchanged, so the edge set

$$
E=\{(j,k):j<k,\ \Omega_{jk}\neq 0\}
$$ {#eq-edge-set}

is identical before and after loading.

The floor $\varepsilon$ also controls the condition number

$$
\kappa(\Omega)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(\Omega)}{\lambda_{\min}(\Omega)}.
$$ {#eq-kappa}

Large loading yields a well-conditioned but weakly dependent network; loading only slightly above $-\lambda_{\min}$ strengthens dependence but can make estimation fragile. Benchmarks should report partial-correlation distributions and $\kappa(\Omega)$, not only the adjacency.

# Conclusions

> DeCovarT uses `power_law` and `stochastic_block_model` skeletons for undirected network structure, then a spectral-shift completion to guarantee $\Omega\succ 0$.

## Further high-dimensional designs

Beyond the families in @tbl-topologies:

-   **Degree-prescribed / configuration** graphs separate degree heterogeneity from preferential-attachment *mechanisms*.
-   **Spatial / geometric** graphs suit spatial transcriptomics or chromatin neighbourhoods.
-   **Differential networks:**
    -   Start from a shared base $G_0$
    -   Controll the differential shift $\Omega_k=\Omega_0+\Delta_k$
    -   Ensure the SPD step
    -   Alternatively,you may vary the *support, weight, and sign* separately [@federicoStructureLearningGene2023; @wuEstimatingHeterogeneousGene2022].
-   **Other distributions,** using the GGM layer as a parameter:
    -   **Latent-variable GGMs** — sparse $\Omega_S$ plus low-rank confounding $Bf_i$.
    -   **Nonparanormal / Gaussian-copula** margins on a latent Gaussian graph.
    -   **Poisson–log-normal / compositional** observation layers on latent log-abundances [@chiquetVariationalInferenceSparse2018].
    -   **Zero-inflated mixture GGMs** with cell-type-specific $(\mu_k,\Omega_k)$ and expression-dependent dropout [@wuEstimatingHeterogeneousGene2022].

## When mean variation should not be omitted

For $X\sim\mathcal{N}_p(\mu,\Omega^{-1})$,

$$
X_j \perp X_k \mid X_{-\{j,k\}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Omega_{jk}=0.
$$ {#eq-ci}

The mean does not appear in @eq-ci, so pure support-recovery studies often set $\mu=0$ after centring [@zhangSILGGMExtensivePackage2018]. That is inadequate when the simulation should mimic expression: pooling groups with distinct $\mu_{g(i)}$ induces between-group covariance

$$
\operatorname{Cov}(X)
=
\operatorname{E}\{\operatorname{Cov}(X\mid g)\}
+
\operatorname{Cov}\{\operatorname{E}(X\mid g)\},
$$ {#eq-law-total-cov}

which can be mistaken for network structure. PLNnetwork therefore includes covariates / offsets, and BLGGM jointly models cell-type means, precisions, and dropout [@chiquetVariationalInferenceSparse2018; @wuEstimatingHeterogeneousGene2022].

@tbl-means crosses mean variations with network changes:

| Mean scenario | Construction | Question tested |
|------------------------|----------------------|---------------------------|
| Null mean | $\mu_i=0$ | Pure graph / precision recovery |
| Sparse DE | Few marker coordinates differ by group | Robustness to phenotype shifts |
| Dense low-rank | $\mu_i = Bz_i$ | Batch / cell-state confounding |
| Mean **and** network heterogeneity | Both $\mu_k$ and $\Omega_k$ vary | Separating DE from differential connectivity |

: Mean designs to cross with topology/precision factors. {#tbl-means}

## Recommended benchmark specification

Use one pipeline for every topology (@eq-benchmark-pipe, @fig-pipeline):

$$
\text{topology}
\rightarrow
\text{signed weights}
\rightarrow
\text{SPD precision}
\rightarrow
\text{mean design}
\rightarrow
\text{latent Gaussian}
\rightarrow
\text{observation model}
$$ {#eq-benchmark-pipe}

| Axis | Suggested levels |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Dimension, namely number of variables (here, genes) | $p \in \{100,500,1000\}$ |
| Topology | ER, band, hub, scale-free, SBM |
| Expected degree | $\approx 2,4,8$ (keep graphs sparse) |
| Edge weights | Constant; signed uniform; G-Wishart |
| Conditioning | Report $\lambda_{\min}$, $\lambda_{\max}$, $\kappa(\Omega)$ |
| Means | Zero; sparse group shifts, driven by cell-type; joint $\mu$–$\Omega$ heterogeneity, for example playing on the *cosine similarity*, or the *condition number*, of the mean profile |

: Compact factorial axes for a reproducible undirected GGM simulation study. {#tbl-benchmark}

**Main insights.** Prefer the uniform spectral shift (@eq-spectral-shift) as the primary SPD step; and add the mean layer **independently** of graph generation.
